Thought: To determine which compound does not participate in conjugate addition with butanamine, I'll need to consider the chemistry of conjugate addition. Conjugate addition typically involves nucleophiles adding to α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds. Butanamine, being a nucleophile, will add to these compounds at the β position. A. But-2-enal is an α,β-unsaturated aldehyde and can participate in conjugate addition.
B. Butenone is an α,β-unsaturated ketone and can participate in conjugate addition.
C. Ethyl but-3-enoate is an α,β-unsaturated ester and can participate in conjugate addition.
D. Propenal is an α,β-unsaturated aldehyde and can participate in conjugate addition.

All options appear to be α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds that can undergo conjugate addition. However, esters like ethyl but-3-enoate are less reactive in conjugate addition compared to aldehydes and ketones.
